---
title: Blank Template
description: Start from an empty Nextly config and define your own schemas.
---

The **Blank** template scaffolds a minimal Nextly project with no collections or singles defined. You get the full Next.js App Router setup, the admin route, the standard environment configuration, and an empty `nextly.config.ts` ready for you to fill in. It's the starting point when you want to design your schema from scratch.

## Scaffold

<Tabs items={["pnpm", "npm", "yarn", "bun"]}>
<Tab value="pnpm">
```bash
pnpm create nextly-app@alpha my-app --template blank
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="npm">
```bash
npx create-nextly-app@alpha my-app --template blank
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="yarn">
```bash
yarn create nextly-app@alpha my-app --template blank
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="bun">
```bash
bun create nextly-app@alpha my-app --template blank
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## What it ships

- **Empty `nextly.config.ts`** with `collections: []` and `singles: []`. Add definitions here as you build.
- **Standard Next.js App Router setup** -- root `layout.tsx`, `globals.css`, a `favicon.ico`, and the home page at `(frontend)/page.tsx`. The landing page is a simple "Welcome" screen with a link into the admin.
- **Generated admin route** at `src/app/admin/[[...params]]/`. The page wires up `RootLayout`, `QueryProvider` and `ErrorBoundary`, and imports `@nextlyhq/admin/style.css`. The layout reads admin branding from `nextly.config.ts` and injects the resulting CSS variables.
- **Health and media routes** under `src/app/api/`, and the admin media library's route at `src/app/admin/api/media/`.
- **Default `next.config.ts`** whose `serverExternalPackages` lists Nextly's server packages and the adapter and driver for the database you chose. See [Project Structure](/docs/getting-started/project-structure) for the full list and what each entry does.
- **Default `.env.example`** with `DB_DIALECT`, `DATABASE_URL`, `NEXTLY_SECRET` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`. Media is stored on local disk until you configure a storage adapter.
- **`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`** with instructions for coding agents working in the project.
- **Skills for coding agents** in `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`, unless you pass `--no-skills`, answer no, or the project installs a different `nextly` release than the skills were checked against. See [Coding agents](/docs/guides/coding-agents).
- **Generated `nextly-types.ts`** stub under `src/types/generated/` so type generation has a destination on first run.

## File tree

```
my-app/
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── (frontend)/
│   │   │   ├── components/
│   │   │   └── page.tsx

│   │   │   ├── [[...params]]/
│   │   │   │   ├── layout.tsx
│   │   │   │   └── page.tsx
│   │   │   └── api/
│   │   │       ├── [[...params]]/
│   │   │       │   └── route.ts
│   │   │       └── media/
│   │   │           └── [[...path]]/
│   │   │               └── route.ts
│   │   ├── api/
│   │   │   ├── health/
│   │   │   │   └── route.ts
│   │   │   └── media/
│   │   │       └── [[...path]]/
│   │   │           └── route.ts
│   │   ├── favicon.ico
│   │   ├── globals.css
│   │   └── layout.tsx
│   ├── lib/
│   │   └── site-url.ts
│   └── types/
│       └── generated/
│           └── nextly-types.ts
├── public/
├── .agents/skills/
├── .claude/skills/
├── .env
├── .env.example
├── AGENTS.md

```
